question: A dealer makes a profit of 50% even after giving a 25% discount on the advertised price of a bike. If he makes a profit of ₹1,290 on the sale of the bike, what is the advertised price (in ₹)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let CP = 100

Profit = 50% ⇒ SP = 150

Discount = 25% ⇒ SP = 75% of MP

⇒ MP = 150 ÷ 0.75 = 200

Profit = 50 ⇒ actual profit = 1290 ⇒ multiply by 25.8 ⇒ MP = 200 × 25.8 = 5160

**∴ Answer = 5160**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Profit = 50%, Discount = 25%, Profit amount = 1290

**Formula used:**

SP = CP × (1 + profit%) and SP = MP × (1 − discount%)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let CP = x

⇒ Profit = 50% ⇒ SP = 1.5x

⇒ Discount = 25% ⇒ SP = 0.75 × MP

⇒ 1.5x = 0.75 × MP

⇒ MP = (1.5x ÷ 0.75) = 2x

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 1.5x − x = 0.5x

⇒ 0.5x = 1290 ⇒ x = 2580

⇒ MP = 2x = 5160

**∴ The correct answer is 5160.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit Formula

Profit = SP − CP and Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

Discount Formula

SP = MP × (1 − discount%)

Assumption Method

Assume CP = 100 to quickly find ratio between MP and CP

Link Between CP and MP

Using SP as common link helps relate CP and MP easily
